securityAssessment: One sequence owns both overview and history updates. The success guard follows JSON completion, and the catch guard rejects obsolete fetch/parser/render failure; stale callbacks do not alter newest loading, successful, or error UI.
Starting a refresh clears previous rows and summary. Filters respect loading/error state and cannot recreate previous payment links or mistake a failed request for an empty history.
The current selected filter applies when the newest result arrives; overview and history derive from the same accepted rows rather than independent competing requests.

Product network scope remains the existing read-only history GET with no-store and unchanged authentication header. No writer, navigation, clipboard, credentials, dependency or dynamic-code sink was added.

The deployment recipe binds one fixed HTML target and old/new hashes, gate inputs, inactive/failed autopilot and MainPID zero, fsynced exact rollback preimage, atomic replacement and unchanged services; no service or database mutation is introduced.
limitations: Bounded timing/diff review only; the existing application and E4/earlier gates are not certified by this result.
Newest means the most recently invoked UI request; this change does not introduce server-side revision or authoritative financial-state validation.
A stalled newest history request can remain loading; this slice adds no deadline or cancellation. A new explicit refresh obtains a newer owner.
Malformed nonarray/null-row/parser cases were tested; this is not a complete schema or preexisting action-URL audit.

No real customer API/data, support message, money, signing, credentials, production or 064A action was performed by this reviewer. Actual Telegram/iOS/WebKit and human/screen-reader acceptance remain unverified.
Predeployment review; final rollout and runtime verification remain primary-agent responsibility.
